senses.gloss: Na-ga (‘not moving’), ‘mountain,’ is a word occurring only in a late book of the Atharvaveda (xix. 8, 1), and then in the Sūtras.

Na-ciketas occurs in the well-known legend of the taittirīya brāhmaṇa (where he is a gotama, the son of vājaśravasa), and in the Kaṭha upaniṣad. His historical reality is extremely doubtful: in the upaniṣad he is called son of āruṇi auddālaki or vājaśravasa, an impossible attribution, and one due only to a desire to give naciketas a connexion with the famous āruṇi.
Foot notes iii. 11, 8.
i. 1, etc. Cf. Geldner, Vedische Studien, 3, 154, n, 1; Weber, Indian Literature, 157; Macdonell, Vedic Mythology, p. 168.
